advances: Necessary second-order condition at an actual fixed-budget maximum in planar support coordinates, with active compatibility rows and cap-pattern branches retained.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Take a common refinement of the planar fans, retaining the linear subspace where each fiber support is linear on its own fan. Fact 074a5bdf8c59720e gives finitely many linear support-convexity and anchored compatibility rows in these coordinates, including the equivalence to actual hull realization. Positivity persists near $h_*$. Each fiber vertex is an intersection of consecutive fixed support lines, hence is linear in the offsets, and the cyclic shoelace formula gives total area as an exact quadratic polynomial. A refinement may insert coinciding vertices without altering the area.

For a given cap on a given integer fiber, a purely base trace is full or empty with constant status. Otherwise add the fixed cutting line and keep the side prescribed by the closed cap. Candidate vertices are the finitely many intersections of pairs of nonparallel lines. They depend affinely on $h$, and their feasibility is determined by finitely many affine inequalities. Subdivide by these signs and, for parallel lines with the same unit normal, their affine offset comparisons. The resulting relatively open cells have a fixed cyclic list of feasible vertices for each full-dimensional truncated polygon, ordered by the incident line normals, and have fixed empty or degenerate status otherwise. On each closure, repeated vertices and zero-length edges are allowed. The area is still the quadratic shoelace polynomial there by continuity of clipped area. These polynomials agree in value on shared faces. Intersect the closures with the actual compatibility rows to obtain the stated cells. This construction also covers inside and outside supporting-edge coincidences, where the polynomial derivatives from different cells can differ.

If the displayed strict acceleration system held, $h(t)=h_*+tv+t^2w/2$ would stay in the chosen cell for all sufficiently small $t>0$: for its active rows either the first coefficient is positive or it is zero and the second coefficient is nonnegative, and the inactive rows retain slack. At a tied budget the second cap coefficient is $(c_jw+q_j(v))/2$, whereas at the other active budgets the first coefficient is strictly negative. The exact polynomials give only $O(t^3)$ further terms on this path. The objective has positive second coefficient and vanishing first coefficient. Thus the actual path is feasible with larger mass, contrary to local maximality.

For the equivalence, put $W=\{w:B_{I(v)}w\ge0\}$. The affine image of $W$ with coordinates $mw+q_0(v)$ and $-c_jw-q_j(v)$ misses the open positive orthant. Separate the two convex sets. The nonzero separator can be oriented as $(\theta,\lambda)\ge0$ since the orthant extends arbitrarily far in each positive coordinate. Its infimum on the open orthant is zero. On the image of $W$ its constant term is nonpositive by $0\in W$; its linear part is nonpositive on $W$ by scaling. The polar formula for a polyhedral cone gives $\theta m-\sum_j\lambda_j c_j=-\eta^\top B_{I(v)}$ with $\eta\ge0$. Conversely this identity and the inequality on the constant term prevent any image point from having all coordinates positive. When the stated $e$ exists, $\theta=0$ would make some $\lambda_j>0$ and would yield $\sum_j\lambda_jc_je=\eta^\top B_{I(v)}e\ge0$, contrary to the strict negative values. Divide all multipliers by $\theta>0$.

In particular a common small Euclidean inner erosion can supply such a direction when the cap-pattern chamber is open, the support chart admits that erosion, and tied cap masses are positive. Anchored compatibility persists because $\sum_z\alpha_z(K_z\ominus tB_2)+tB_2\subseteq\sum_z\alpha_zK_z\subseteq K_p$ at each anchored convex combination. For polygons whose original facets persist, each original unit support offset decreases by $t$. A positive fixed cap either contains an entire positive fiber or properly cuts a positive fiber in which a positive length of an old facet lies strictly inside the cap. In either case a positive first-order area is lost in that cap by erosion. At a cap-pattern boundary, the resulting direction need not stay in a chosen cell, so the conditional normalization above is needed there.
statement:
On a finite lattice-complete base, fix planar positive polygonal fibers with fixed normal fans. Near a given compatible support array $h_*$, fix finitely many ambient closed caps and upper cap budgets. Suppose $h_*$ locally maximizes total mixed area subject to those budgets among actual compatible arrays of the chart. The support chart admits a finite closed polyhedral subdivision on which the total area $M$ and the fixed cap masses $C_j$ are exact quadratic polynomials. In a cell $B h\ge b$ containing $h_*$, write $I$ for its active rows, $J$ for active budgets, $m=DM(h_*)$, $c_j=DC_j(h_*)$ using that cell's polynomial, and $q_0(v)=D^2M[v,v]$, $q_j(v)=D^2C_j[v,v]$.

For each $v$ with $B_Iv\ge0$, $c_jv\le0$ on $J$, and $mv=0$, set $I(v)=\{i\in I:B_iv=0\}$ and $J(v)=\{j\in J:c_jv=0\}$. There is no $w$ satisfying
$$
B_{I(v)}w\ge0,\qquad c_jw+q_j(v)<0\ (j\in J(v)),\qquad mw+q_0(v)>0.
$$
Equivalently there are $\theta,\lambda_j,\eta_i\ge0$ with $\theta+\sum_j\lambda_j>0$ such that
$$
\theta m=\sum_{j\in J(v)}\lambda_jc_j-\eta^\top B_{I(v)},\qquad
\theta q_0(v)-\sum_{j\in J(v)}\lambda_jq_j(v)\le0.
$$
If some $e$ satisfies $B_{I(v)}e\ge0$ and $c_je<0$ for every tied budget, one can take $\theta=1$. The stress may depend on the cell and on $v$.
